provenance.instrument: West Manheim Township Zoning Ordinance of 2009 (Chapter 270 Zoning, Ord. No. 7-2009 of 9-3-2009, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WE3200, Township of West Manheim (270-1: 'Zoning Map, West Manheim Township, York County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and area tables are text in Parts 4 and 5. Attachments are the zoning map, the overlay map and sign tables. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 141 and the Floodplain Protection Overlay (270-63 to 270-66). New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 07-29-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' Ord. No. 2-2026 of 7-29-2026 (TND district and 270-15) is codified
checks: 'ECHO housing' is 'An additional temporary dwelling unit placed on a property for occupancy by either an elderly, handicapped, or disabled person related by blood, marriage, adoption or in foster care to the occupants of the principal dwelling' (270-13). It is a conditional use in the Residential, Suburban Residential and Farming districts (270-21D(1), 270-27D(1), 270-45E(2)). The Board of Supervisors decides

270-109A also covers an 'apartment addition': the lot needs at least one acre. At least one occupant must be 62 or older, or handicapped or disabled, and related to the occupants of the house. At most two people may live there (270-109A(1), (4), (5))
The unit must meet the setbacks for principal uses, and the house, accessory structures and the unit together may not exceed the district's lot coverage (270-109A(3), (8))

One added all-weather off-street space beyond the house's three (270-109A(7), 270-197). The Zoning Officer issues a temporary use and occupancy permit that is renewed every year. The unit must be removed or made a permitted use within 12 months after no qualifying person lives there (270-109A(9), (10))

The Traditional Neighborhood Development district does not list ECHO housing. It allows 'Accessory uses that are customarily accessory under the Residential (R) District regulations' (270-31A(2)). Whether that reaches ECHO housing is not settled. The Commercial/Industrial district permits no dwelling

Residential conversion: a two-family conversion of a single-family detached dwelling that existed on the effective date of the chapter (Ord. No. 7-2009, adopted 9-3-2009) is a special exception in Residential, Suburban Residential and TND. One unit must be owner-occupied, and there may be no extensions or outside changes that alter the residential character (270-163)

Two-family dwellings are permitted by right in Residential and Suburban Residential with centralized water and sewer: 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft of width per dwelling unit (270-19B(5), 270-22, 270-25B(7), 270-28)

A lot in Residential or Suburban Residential 'shall not include more than one principal use and shall not include more than one principal building unless specifically permitted by this chapter' (270-83B(1))

Accessory buildings: over 250 sq ft or 12 ft tall they meet the principal building setbacks. They must be 10 ft from the house, may cover at most 10% of the net lot area in Residential, Suburban Residential and Farming, and may be at most 1 1/2 stories or 20 ft there (270-90A, C, D, E)

Natural Features Overlay: no structures on slopes of 25% or more, within 25 ft of a watercourse (and nearby alluvial soils, springs and 25% slopes within 50 ft), or in or within 25 ft of a wetland (270-58, 270-59, 270-61). The overlays are set from a survey at the time of the permit

Floodplain (Chapter 141): new residential construction needs the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. In an AE area without a floodway no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank unless DEP's regional office issues a permit. In a floodway no new construction without a DEP permit and no rise in flood levels, and manufactured homes are prohibited (141-18, 141-23A, 141-27A)
Unlisted uses are prohibited unless the Zoning Hearing Board allows one as a special exception that is 'closely similar in external impacts and character to uses permitted in that district' (270-7)
No use variance bar was found. The Zoning Hearing Board decides variances on the findings of 270-232B
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Manheim Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Article I, 270-14 to 270-17, Parts 4 and 5, Part 6 to 270-74, Part 7 Articles XIV to XVI, 270-162, 270-163, 270-197, 270-232, Chapter 141 to 141-33 and code searches, including the definitions of ECHO housing, residential conversion, family and dwelling unit. Not read: the rest of 270-13 (including lot coverage), 270-111 to 270-161 and 270-164 to 270-177 (including 270-131 two-family dwellings), Article XVIII nonconformities, Parts 8 to 11 except 270-197 (including the conditional use procedure and 270-220B temporary use permits), 270-233 and Article XIII historic overlay.

term.note: Searched for in-law, accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, second dwelling, ECHO, caretaker, living quarters, guest house, garage apartment, extended family, household employee, conversion, servant and two-family. 270-109A also names an 'apartment addition'

status.note: A conditional use for a relative of the occupants of the house who is 62 or older, handicapped or disabled

scope_districts.note: ECHO housing is a listed conditional use in these three districts

status_outside.note: TND and Commercial/Industrial do not list ECHO housing

path.note: The Board of Supervisors decides a conditional use after a public hearing (MPC 913.2). The conditional use procedure in Part 11 was not read

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 270-232B

unlisted_use_path.note: 'If a use clearly is not permitted by right, as a special exception use, or as a conditional use by this chapter within any zoning district, the use is prohibited', except that the Zoning Hearing Board may allow it as a special exception on the findings of 270-7A to D. Two-family dwellings are listed by right in Residential and Suburban Residential and in an approved TND, so a second unit there may be read as that use, not an unlisted one

unlisted_use_scope.quote: The proposed use would be closely similar in external impacts and character to uses permitted in that district

value.name: Two-family residential conversion
value.conditions: 'The structure must be a single-family detached dwelling that existed on the effective date of this chapter.' 'At least one of the dwelling units shall be owner-occupied.' Approved water and sewage, no extensions or outside changes that alter the residential character except fire escapes, and any land development approval (270-163A to F). Two spaces per dwelling unit (270-197)

requires.condition: The house existed on the effective date of the chapter (Ord. No. 7-2009, adopted 9-3-2009)
One of the two units is owner-occupied

value.note: A unit inside the existing house. Not an ADU and not tied to relatives

value.name: Two-family dwelling (Residential, Suburban Residential)
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling needs centralized water and centralized sewer, 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft of width per dwelling unit, side yards of 10 ft, a rear yard of 25 ft and lot coverage of at most 60%. 'Not permitted' with one utility or none. Three spaces per dwelling unit (270-22, 270-28, 270-197)
value.note: A building with two units. Whether an existing house may become one without the conversion rules of 270-163 is not settled. 270-131 was not read

value.name: Apartment residential conversion
value.conditions: 'The building must have been constructed prior to the effective date of this chapter.' Each unit meets the floor area for multifamily dwellings, with approved water and sewage and any land development approval (270-162). Three spaces per unit (270-197)

requires.condition: The building was built before the effective date of the chapter (Ord. No. 7-2009, adopted 9-3-2009)

value.note: The code does not say how many units an apartment conversion makes

min_lot_sqft.note: 'The minimum lot area shall be one acre.'

historic_bypass.note: Article XIII (Historic Preservation Overlay) was not read. No historic path for a second unit was found

districts_in_doubt.note: TND lists no ECHO housing but allows 'Accessory uses that are customarily accessory under the Residential (R) District regulations'. Every new principal use there must be part of an approved TND master plan (270-31A, 270-33)

value.condition: 'The ECHO housing unit or apartment addition shall only be occupied by at least one person who is at least 62 years old, or is handicapped or disabled, and is related to the occupants of the principal dwelling by blood, marriage or adoption.' At most two people.

A temporary use and occupancy permit, renewed every year. The unit must be removed or 'reestablished as a use permitted in the district within 12 months after it is no longer occupied by a person who qualifies for the use'.
The applicant shows that approved sewage disposal and water supply will be used. The Township Sewage Enforcement Officer verifies existing on-lot sewage systems.
The house, existing accessory structures and the ECHO unit or apartment addition together may not exceed the district's maximum lot coverage.

Conservation subdivision (required for new residential subdivisions of 15 acres or more in Residential, optional below): lots of 7,500 sq ft with both utilities, front 40 ft, side 10 ft, rear 20 ft and lot coverage 60%.
On slopes of 25% or more only uses that 'do not require structures' are permitted. No part of a lot with such slopes counts toward the minimum lot size.
overlays: Steep Slope Protection Overlay (slopes of 25% or more)

value.condition: In the Stream Protection Overlay (all land within 25 ft of a watercourse, plus alluvial soils, springs and 25% slopes within 50 ft of it) only uses that 'do not require building(s), fill or storage of materials and equipment' are permitted.
In the Wetland Protection Overlay (in or within 25 ft of a wetland) only uses that 'do not require structures, fill or storage of materials and equipment' are allowed.
Within any floodway area 'manufactured homes shall be prohibited' unless a variance is obtained under Chapter 141, Article VIII.

disputed_by.note: An ECHO unit is a dwelling unit 'placed on a property', not always a manufactured home. A unit that is not a manufactured home is not reached by this bar, but 141-18A still allows no new construction in a floodway without a DEP permit and a showing of no rise in flood levels

value.condition: In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office' (DEP).

In an identified floodplain area new residential construction needs the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. In a floodway no new construction without a DEP permit and a showing of no rise in flood levels. An accessory structure that is not elevated may not be used for human habitation.

types_allowed.note: An ECHO unit is 'placed on a property'. 270-109A also covers an 'apartment addition'

types_not_addressed.note: 270-109A names an ECHO housing unit or an apartment addition only. A unit inside the house or in a garage is not named. A two-family conversion of the house is a separate special exception

value.detached_new: ECHO housing unit placed on the lot

max_sqft.note: No size cap. The unit must meet the minimum habitable floor area of 270-86 (IBC section 1208)

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'The ECHO housing unit or apartment addition shall adhere to setback requirements for principal uses.'

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'all other accessory buildings in the Residential, Suburban Residential, and Farming Zoning Districts shall not be higher than 1 1/2 stories or 20 feet, whichever is less'

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: 270-109A treats the unit like a principal use for setbacks and says nothing of height. Whether the accessory building height binds it is not settled

separation_ft.note: 'An accessory building shall be no less than 10 feet from the principal building.' Whether an ECHO unit is an accessory building is not settled

value.where: An accessory building over 250 sq ft or 12 ft tall meets the principal building setbacks. Only a smaller one may stand 5 ft from a lot line. The ECHO unit itself meets the setbacks for principal uses (270-109A(8))

An ECHO unit placed as a detached building in Farming meets the setbacks for principal uses (270-109A(8)), which grow with the lot: side 10 ft and rear 25 ft on one acre or less, side 20 ft and rear 25 ft over one acre up to two acres, side 30 ft and rear 40 ft over two acres. The side and rear figures shown for a detached unit are those for one acre or less
An accessory building, or all of them together, may cover at most 10% of the net lot area in Residential, Suburban Residential and Farming (farm buildings excepted)

occupancy.value: At least one person who is 62 or older, or handicapped or disabled, and related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption. At most two people

owner_occupancy.note: No owner rule. The occupants must be related to the occupants of the house

max_adus.note: 'An additional temporary dwelling unit'. No number is stated

spaces_required.note: 'A minimum of one all-weather, off-street parking space ... shall be provided for the ECHO housing unit or apartment addition, in addition to that required for the principal dwelling.' The schedule lists ECHO housing as 'Per ECHO housing unit' (270-197)

total_on_site.note: Three for a single-family detached dwelling and one for the ECHO unit

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling with both utilities (centralized water and centralized sewer). 80 ft wide

setback_front_ft.note: '50 arterial, 40 collector and local'. On an arterial street the front setback is 50 ft

setback_side_ft.note: 10 ft with both utilities or one, 20 ft with neither

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage (percent)'. The definition of lot coverage in 270-13 was not read, so whether it counts paving is not settled

utility_rows.note: 270-23A and 270-29A require centralized water and sewer for principal nonagricultural uses in the growth area. Without them a use is a conditional use (270-81B)

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling with both utilities (centralized water and centralized sewer). 80 ft wide

setback_front_ft.note: '50 arterial, 40 collector and local'. On an arterial street the front setback is 50 ft

setback_side_ft.note: 10 ft with both utilities or one, 20 ft with neither

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage (percent)'. The definition of lot coverage in 270-13 was not read, so whether it counts paving is not settled

utility_rows.note: 270-23A and 270-29A require centralized water and sewer for principal nonagricultural uses in the growth area. Without them a use is a conditional use (270-81B)

min_lot_sqft.note: One acre for all uses, 200 ft wide. The maximum lot area is two acres unless more is needed for the driveway or on-site water and sewage (270-46 notes 1 to 3). New lots also count against the parent tract's development allotments (270-47A)

setback_side_ft.note: On a lot of one acre or less. 20 ft over one acre up to two acres, 30 ft over two acres

setback_rear_ft.note: On a lot of two acres or less. 40 ft over two acres

yard_tiers.note: 'Less Than or Equal to 1 Acre', 'Greater Than 1 Acre to Less Than or Equal to 2 Acres', 'Greater Than 2 Acres'

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage (percent)'. The definition of lot coverage in 270-13 was not read, so whether it counts paving is not settled
